findings.message: The hook is registered at `stages: [manual]`, and nothing in this PR invokes it from a CI workflow — so the packaging check only runs when someone remembers the `prek run --hook-stage manual` incantation from the README. What is meant to catch a broken tarball before release? Either wire it into a CI job (release/nightly is fine given the npm install cost) or say in the README which pipeline owns it.

`Object.values(conditions)` only flattens one level, so a nested conditional export — `{"import": {"types": "./dist/index.d.ts", "default": "./dist/index.js"}}`, the shape people reach for first — yields objects and blows up in the `target.replace` on the next line with an opaque `TypeError`. That contradicts the docstring's promise that new export shapes extend the check rather than escaping it; recurse over nested condition objects, or fail with a message that names the offending subpath.
